Biology · Software · Systems

# Hi, I’m Dalton.

::: {.about-lead}
I study molecular biology at Brigham Young University and build computational tools for exploring biological questions.
:::

::: {.about-muted}
My interests sit somewhere between bacteriophage genomics, scientific software, and the systems that make research possible. I like understanding how things work—and building tools that make them easier to understand.
:::

:::

::: {.about-section}

## Connecting biology and computation

I’m especially interested in bacteriophages and what we can learn by comparing their genomes. My work involves genome annotation, comparative analysis, and developing tools to organize, explore, and visualize the results.

The computational side matters to me for more than speed. I want an analysis to be understandable: what went into it, which decisions shaped it, and how someone else could reproduce it.

::: {.about-note}
I enjoy the space between a biological question and a working tool: turning an idea into an analysis, a visualization, or a workflow someone can actually use.
:::

:::

::: {.about-section}

## What I’m building

::: {.about-grid}

::: {.about-card}

::: {.about-label}
Scientific workflows
:::

### Phantom

A Snakemake-based workflow for phage analysis, bringing computational steps into a more organized and reproducible process.

The project brings together my interests in genomics, workflow design, and scientific software development.

:::

::: {.about-card}

::: {.about-label}
Analysis & visualization
:::

### Tools for understanding genomes

R and Python tools for phage visualization and post-annotation analysis.

I’m interested in making results easier to investigate—not just generating output, but helping people see relationships and ask useful follow-up questions.

:::

::: {.about-card .about-wide}

::: {.about-label}
Infrastructure & experimentation
:::

### A homelab that keeps growing

I build and manage Linux servers, virtual machines, containers, and self-hosted services. It’s a practical environment for learning about networking, automation, and the infrastructure behind the software I use.

It’s also where “I wonder if I could…” tends to become a weekend project.

:::

:::
:::

::: {.about-section}

These are the areas I work in and the tools I use across research, software projects, and infrastructure.

:::

:::
:::

::: {.about-section}

## What I’m learning next

I’m strengthening the mathematical and computational foundations behind my work, particularly statistics, probability, linear algebra, and machine learning.

I’m also exploring:

- Systems biology and mathematical modeling
- Python package design and software testing
- R package and Bioconductor development
- Cybersecurity and network visibility
- Kubernetes, GitOps, and infrastructure automation

I like learning through projects: finding a problem worth solving, building a first version, and improving it as I understand the problem better.

:::

::: {.about-section}

## Beyond the technical side

Not everything I do belongs in a terminal.

I enjoy poetry, music, anime, and games. I also like working with electronics and repurposed hardware—projects where there’s something physical to experiment with alongside the code.

This site brings those interests together: part research notebook, part project portfolio, and part place to write about whatever has caught my attention.

:::

:::
